scenarios.title: Angle the carrier to the wall
scenarios.objective: Use an inside approach that guides Gold 1 away from the middle
scenarios.briefing: Navy attacks Gold’s net and defends Navy’s net. Gold 1 carries on the right side toward Navy’s blue line. YOU starts inside; D1 is behind and Gold 2 trails wide.
cues: Gold 1 carries wide right toward the blue line.
YOU are inside the carrier; D1 is behind.

questions.prompt: Where is Gold 1 carrying?

options.text: Along the right side toward the blue line
Across the middle toward the left side

questions.explanation: Gold 1’s route gives YOU an inside angle to guide wide; a different route needs a different approach.

questions.prompt: Which two relationships fit the angling goal?

options.text: The wall remains the easier escape

questions.explanation: An inside position protects middle while the wall is the lower-risk direction; crossing behind loses the steering angle.

questions.prompt: Order one angling approach.

options.text: Close from inside while matching the route

questions.explanation: The carrier’s route controls approach; matching it protects middle; D1’s support gives the finish a second defender.

questions.prompt: Move YOU inside and slightly ahead of Gold 1 to show the angle.
questions.explanation: The inside-ahead position protects middle and leaves Gold 1 the wall; if Gold 1 slows or passes, update rather than skating past.

questions.prompt: If Gold 1 passes inside to Gold 2, what deserves attention?

options.text: Whether Gold 2 threatens middle and D1 can help
Angling the player who no longer has the puck

questions.explanation: The pass changes carrier and inside threat, so switch to Gold 2 and D1; if Gold 2 is covered, recovery changes again.

questions.prompt: Why can a fast approach be unhelpful here?
questions.explanation: Speed without an inside angle can carry YOU past Gold 1 and give up middle, so match the route and keep support connected; if the carrier slows, close under control.

scenarios.title: Backcheck the middle before the puck
scenarios.objective: Recover through the middle so the most dangerous attacker stays in view
scenarios.briefing: Navy attacks Gold’s net and defends Navy’s net. Gold 1 carries into the right zone with Gold 2 cutting middle. YOU is the backchecking forward; D1 defends puck side.
cues: Gold 2 cuts through middle without the puck.
D1 is on Gold 1’s puck side; YOU recover behind.

questions.prompt: Which attacker is the inside support threat?
questions.explanation: Gold 2’s middle cut makes that player the inside threat while D1 engages the carrier; if Gold 2 changes lane, recovery changes.

questions.prompt: Which two reads make your backcheck useful?
questions.explanation: The middle route identifies danger and D1’s position tells you whether to support inside; blind wide skating can miss the threat.

questions.prompt: Arrange one middle-lane backcheck.

options.text: Recover through middle toward the net

questions.explanation: Seeing Gold 2 prevents a puck-only chase; middle recovery protects net; communication avoids two defenders following Gold 1.

questions.prompt: Move YOU into the middle lane between Gold 2 and the Navy net.
questions.explanation: The middle position protects the direct threat and lets YOU arrive underneath Gold 2; if D1 loses the carrier, keep both threats visible.

questions.prompt: If Gold 2 receives before you arrive, what changes?

options.text: Gold 2 becomes carrier and D1’s coverage must be reassessed
Your original route stays correct automatically
The net-side lane can be abandoned

questions.explanation: The reception changes the threat, so update carrier and roles; if Gold 2 is contained, recover to the next danger.

questions.prompt: How can you tell you are helping D1 rather than duplicating D1?
questions.explanation: Cover the middle attacker while D1 faces the carrier, then call when roles change; if both chase one puck, another lane is open.

scenarios.title: Cover the far-side low slot
scenarios.objective: Keep the far-side low attacker and puck-side pressure in one picture
scenarios.briefing: Navy attacks Gold’s net and defends Navy’s net. Gold 1 has the puck on the left half wall. Gold 2 waits in the far-side low slot. YOU is weak side; D1 is below the puck.
cues: Gold 2 is the far-side low attacker.
Gold 1 owns puck on the left half wall; YOU are weak side.

questions.prompt: Who is the off-puck low threat?
questions.explanation: Gold 2 is the visible far-side attacker, so YOU first keeps that lane in view; if Gold 2 rises, update.

questions.prompt: Which two things should YOU keep in view?
questions.explanation: The low threat and carrier side connect the weak-side read; staring only at puck can lose backdoor lane.

questions.prompt: Arrange one weak-side coverage scan.

options.text: See whether D1 has puck-side lane

questions.explanation: Gold 2’s route sets danger; D1’s position shows what is covered; final position protects the open net-side lane.

questions.prompt: Move YOU closer to the low slot while staying between Gold 2 and the Navy net.
questions.explanation: The net-side position keeps Gold 2 visible and still sees Gold 1; if Gold 2 moves high, follow the new danger.

questions.prompt: Gold 2 cuts from the far-side low slot toward the net. What must YOU update?

options.text: The lane between Gold 2 and the Navy net
The old spot even if Gold 2 moves
Only Gold 1’s stick, not the low lane

questions.explanation: Gold 2’s movement changes the net-side lane, so YOU updates the coverage relationship before looking back to Gold 1; if the lane closes, communicate the handoff.

questions.prompt: How can you check the half wall without forgetting Gold 2?
questions.explanation: Use a shoulder check that keeps Gold 2 between you and the net, then glance puck-side; if Gold 2 cuts behind, net-side lane wins.

scenarios.title: Choose the second rebound job
scenarios.objective: Separate the first rebound player from the supporting defender’s job
scenarios.briefing: Navy attacks Gold’s net and defends Navy’s net. Gold 1 shoots from the right circle. The rebound is loose below the crease; D1 is closest and YOU is net-side of Gold 2.
cues: The puck is loose below the crease after Gold 1’s shot.
D1 is closest; Gold 2 is net-side of YOU.

questions.prompt: Who is closest to the loose rebound?
questions.explanation: D1 is nearest, so YOU reads the next threat and support lane; if D1 misses it, the job changes.

questions.prompt: Which two cues shape YOU’s second job?

options.text: The original shooting lane, without checking Gold 2 or D1

questions.explanation: Gold 2 may be the scoring threat while D1 attacks puck, so YOU balances routes; jersey number does not locate danger.

questions.prompt: Arrange one second-player rebound read.
questions.explanation: Puck location tells you whether D1 can reach; confirming D1 frees YOU to cover; the second job protects the attacker.

questions.prompt: Move YOU between Gold 2 and the Navy net while D1 attacks the rebound.
questions.explanation: The net-side position protects Gold 2 and leaves D1 room; if D1 loses the race, reassess possession.

questions.prompt: If D1 gains clear control, what should YOU reassess?

options.text: Whether Gold 2 remains the nearest uncovered attacker

questions.explanation: D1’s control changes the puck threat, so keep Gold 2 covered and prepare an outlet; if Gold 2 leaves, scan next lane.

questions.prompt: Why must a rebound read distinguish loose from controlled?
questions.explanation: A loose puck requires a race, while control changes the job to coverage and support; if goalie or D1 covers it, chasing the old rebound wastes position.

scenarios.title: Recover after the pinch misses
scenarios.objective: Protect the middle after D1’s pinch fails and Gold 1 exits wide
scenarios.briefing: Navy attacks Gold’s net and defends Navy’s net. D1 pinched at the right blue line but Gold 1 won the puck and exits along the wall. YOU is nearest recovering forward; Gold 2 cuts inside.
cues: D1’s pinch did not gain possession; Gold 1 has puck on the right wall.

questions.explanation: Possession was lost, so priority moves from attack to recovery; if Navy regains it, update.

questions.prompt: Which two dangers should YOU read?

options.text: Whether an empty wall lane means Gold 1 cannot pass

questions.explanation: Gold 1 carries while Gold 2 offers inside support, so recover middle and communicate; bench is irrelevant.

questions.prompt: Arrange one failed-pinch recovery.

options.text: Angle Gold 1 after middle is protected

questions.explanation: Turnover updates carrier; inside recovery protects net; once middle is covered, wall carrier can be angled.

questions.prompt: Move YOU into the inside recovery lane below Gold 2.
questions.explanation: The inside position protects the direct route and lets YOU angle Gold 1 later; if Gold 2 receives, step to new threat.

questions.prompt: If Gold 2 receives before you arrive, what is your priority?

options.text: Contain Gold 2 as carrier and keep net-side lane closed

questions.explanation: The reception changes who can attack net, so switch scan and contain; if Gold 2 is covered, return to next threat.

questions.prompt: Why does the failed pinch change your first skating lane?
questions.explanation: Possession moved to Gold and inside support is closer to net, so middle recovery protects the highest-risk route; if Navy recovers, transition roles change.

findings.issue: Every new-scene briefing uses '+x' and '-x' axis notation in player-facing text. U13 players should receive named-net language.
findings.evidence: All 25 exp26b-u13 briefings begin with 'Navy attacks the +x end and Gold attacks the -x end.'
findings.recommendedChange: Replace that sentence in each new briefing with 'Navy attacks Gold's net and defends Navy's net.' Preserve the actual net and actor geometry while removing coordinate notation from the player-facing scene.

findings.issue: These prompts duplicate prompts already used elsewhere in the frozen batch, reducing scene-specific coaching value.
findings.evidence: b013-q5 repeats exp26-u13-016-q5; b016-q4 repeats b012-q4; b016-q5 repeats exp26-u13-019-q5.
findings.recommendedChange: Rewrite b013-q5 around the far-side low-slot lane update; rewrite b016-q4 around keeping Gold 2 and Gold 1 in view during the interception; rewrite b016-q5 around reassessing support after D1 wins the puck back. Keep each reference and explanation specific to its own scene.

findings.issue: The listed distractors are unrelated trivia, impossible guarantees, or automatic-certainty claims rather than credible U13 hockey decisions.
findings.evidence: Examples include 'The original faceoff result', 'Whether the bench door is open', 'The score from a previous game', 'A guaranteed open net', 'That the shot must go in', 'The goalie’s save is guaranteed', 'Changed teams', and 'The neutral-zone bench'.
findings.recommendedChange: Replace each affected distractor with a plausible nearby choice involving pressure route, support lane, puck protection, coverage handoff, or a conditional branch in that scene. Avoid guaranteed outcomes, irrelevant bench/game trivia, and choices that no player could reasonably select in the shown play.
